option_description: Whether the server delivers a restrictive Content-Security-Policy response header that constrains script/object/frame sources, providing the second-layer defense against reflected/stored/DOM XSS.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cross-site scripting / DOM script injection" — the exposure fires when this is false (the CSP header is absent), leaving the page's XSS surface unmitigated at the policy layer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Content-Security-Policy response header from the app's document response.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-...'; object-src 'none' (secure / true) vs no header (insecure / false)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the document request's response headers in browser DevTools.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > select the document request > Response Headers > content-security-policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Restrictive policy present (secure / true) vs missing (insecure / false)

option_description: Whether the CSP's script-src/default-src permits 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', or a wildcard, which would neutralize the CSP as an XSS control even when a header is present.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cross-site scripting / DOM script injection" — the exposure fires when this is true, because a CSP that allows unsafe-inline/eval no longer blocks injected script.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the CSP header and inspect its script-src/default-src directives for the dangerous keywords.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy WITHOUT 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval' and without default-src * (secure / false) vs those tokens present (insecure / true)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the CSP in DevTools and confirm script-src excludes unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval (uses nonces/hashes instead).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > document request > Response Headers > content-security-policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: script-src uses 'nonce-...'/'sha256-...' with no 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval' (secure / false) vs permissive (insecure / true)

option_description: Whether the CSP enforces Trusted Types (require-trusted-types-for 'script'), forcing dangerous DOM sinks (innerHTML, eval) through a sanitizing policy to mitigate DOM-based XSS.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cross-site scripting / DOM script injection" — the exposure fires when this is false, leaving DOM XSS sinks unguarded.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether the CSP header carries the require-trusted-types-for directive.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: require-trusted-types-for (present = secure / true) vs no match (not enforced / false)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN Content-Security-Policy header reference (Trusted Types directives)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the CSP in DevTools for the trusted-types and require-trusted-types-for directives.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > document request > Response Headers > content-security-policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: require-trusted-types-for 'script' present (secure / true) vs absent (false)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN Content-Security-Policy header reference (Trusted Types directives)

option_description: Whether all untrusted data is rendered via context-aware output encoding / auto-escaping templating, with no raw innerHTML/document.write/dangerouslySetInnerHTML/v-html of user data — the foundational first-layer XSS defense.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cross-site scripting / DOM script injection" — the exposure fires when this is false, because user data reaches a DOM sink unsanitized.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the client source for dangerous DOM sinks and trace whether untrusted data flows into them unsanitized.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No untrusted data flows into these sinks unsanitized (secure / true) vs user-controlled values assigned to innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML (insecure XSS sink / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Cross-Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet; OWASP Top 10 A03 Injection

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review templates/components to confirm untrusted data is rendered via auto-escaping framework bindings with DOMPurify on any HTML.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All dynamic data auto-escaped, DOMPurify on raw HTML (secure / true) vs raw interpolation of user data (false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Cross-Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet; OWASP Top 10 A03 Injection

option_description: Whether the server sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, stopping the browser from MIME-sniffing responses into executable types.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cross-site scripting / DOM script injection" — the exposure fires when this is false (header absent), enabling MIME-sniffing of user-controlled content into script.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the X-Content-Type-Options response header.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: x-content-type-options: nosniff (secure / true) vs absent (insecure / false)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the document response headers in DevTools for the nosniff directive.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > document request > Response Headers > x-content-type-options
how_to_obtain.expected_output: nosniff present (secure / true) vs absent (false)

option_description: Whether a session token, JWT, refresh token, or PII is persisted in localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB or any other JavaScript-readable client storage (true = insecure).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for both "Token / session theft from insecure client storage" and "Sensitive data cached / persisted client-side" — both exposures fire when this is true, because injected script or a hostile extension can read and replay the token / harvest PII.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect client storage in DevTools for any token or PII presence after authenticating.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Application > Storage > Local Storage / Session Storage / IndexedDB
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No JWT/refresh token or PII present (secure / false) vs token/PII visible in JS-readable storage (insecure / true)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode the access token and confirm tokens are held in HttpOnly cookies / a BFF pattern rather than JS-readable storage.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Decode the access token (jwt.io / DevTools) and check DevTools > Application > Local/Session Storage for any token presence
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No token in JS-readable storage (secure / false) vs token in localStorage (insecure / true)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 JSON Web Token Best Current Practices; OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether the session/auth cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute, forbidding JavaScript (document.cookie) access to the token.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Token / session theft from insecure client storage" — the exposure fires when this is false, because injected script can read and exfiltrate the session token via document.cookie.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Set-Cookie header from the login/session response and check for the HttpOnly attribute.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=... (secure / true) vs no HttpOnly flag (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN Set-Cookie header reference; OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the HttpOnly column for the session cookie in DevTools.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Application > Storage > Cookies — check HttpOnly column
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HttpOnly checked for the session cookie (secure / true) vs unchecked (insecure / false)

option_description: Whether the session cookie carries the Secure attribute so it is only transmitted over HTTPS, preventing leakage to a network attacker over cleartext.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for both "Token / session theft from insecure client storage" and "Session hijacking over insecure transport / mixed content" — both fire when this is false, because the cookie can leak over cleartext and be replayed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Set-Cookie header and check for the Secure attribute.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure (present = secure / true) vs no match (insecure / false)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Secure column for the session cookie in DevTools.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Application > Storage > Cookies — check Secure column
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure checked for the session cookie (secure / true) vs unchecked (insecure / false)

option_description: The SameSite attribute value on the session cookie (Strict, Lax, or None), controlling whether the cookie is sent on cross-site requests.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Token / session theft from insecure client storage" — the exposure fires when this equals 'None' (cookie sent cross-site, widening replay/CSRF surface); 'Strict' and 'Lax' are the non-firing secure values.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Set-Cookie header and read the SameSite= value.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SameSite=Strict/Lax (secure) vs SameSite missing or =None (weaker / firing)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the SameSite column for the session cookie in DevTools.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Application > Storage > Cookies — read SameSite column
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Strict or Lax (secure) vs None (firing)

option_description: Whether access tokens delivered to the client are short-lived (minutes) with refresh-token rotation and server-side revocation.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Token / session theft from insecure client storage" — the exposure fires when this is false, because a stolen long-lived token remains valid long enough to hijack the account and cannot be revoked.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode the access token and read its exp claim; confirm token lifetime is short and rotation/revocation is in place.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Decode the access token (jwt.io / DevTools) and read the exp claim; check DevTools > Application > Local/Session Storage for any token presence
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Short exp (minutes), no token in JS-readable storage (secure / true) vs long exp and token in localStorage (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 JSON Web Token Best Current Practices; OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm refresh-token rotation and server-side revocation are configured in the identity/session layer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Refresh-token rotation + server-side revocation enabled (secure / true) vs non-revocable long-lived bearer tokens (false)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 JSON Web Token Best Current Practices; OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether the application sends a Strict-Transport-Security response header with a long max-age and includeSubDomains, forcing the browser onto HTTPS.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Session hijacking over insecure transport / mixed content" — the exposure fires when this is false (missing header or max-age=0), allowing SSL-strip/downgrade so cookies/tokens travel in cleartext.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Strict-Transport-Security response header.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains (secure / true) vs absent / max-age=0 (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 6797 HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS); OWASP Secure Headers Project

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the document response headers in DevTools for the HSTS header and its max-age.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > document request > Response Headers > strict-transport-security
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Long max-age with includeSubDomains (secure / true) vs absent or max-age=0 (false)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 6797 HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS); OWASP Secure Headers Project

option_description: Whether the Content-Security-Policy includes the upgrade-insecure-requests directive, instructing the browser to rewrite http:// subresource requests to https://.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Session hijacking over insecure transport / mixed content" — the exposure fires when this is false, leaving the page reliant on no-mixed-content discipline and exposed to cleartext downgrade of subresources.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether the CSP header carries the upgrade-insecure-requests directive.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: upgrade-insecure-requests present (secure / true) vs absent (false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secure Headers Project (recommended CSP); MDN Content-Security-Policy header reference

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the CSP in DevTools and confirm the upgrade-insecure-requests directive is present.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > document request > Response Headers > content-security-policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Directive present (secure / true) vs absent (false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secure Headers Project (recommended CSP); MDN Content-Security-Policy header reference

option_description: Whether the page actually references http:// scripts, iframes, or other active subresources (active mixed content). True is the insecure state.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Session hijacking over insecure transport / mixed content" — the exposure fires when this is true, because an attacker can read/modify the downgraded cleartext portion and ride the session even with HSTS present.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Load the page and watch the DevTools Console / Security panel for mixed-content warnings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Console / Security panel — look for 'Mixed Content' warnings on page load
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No mixed-content warnings (secure / false) vs blocked/upgraded http subresource warnings (insecure source present / true)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the rendered HTML for hardcoded http:// active subresources.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No http:// active subresources (secure / false) vs http:// script/iframe references (insecure / true)

option_description: Whether every cross-origin/CDN <script> and <link> tag carries a Subresource Integrity (integrity='sha384-...') attribute plus crossorigin, so the browser rejects a tampered/swapped third-party resource.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Client-side supply-chain compromise (CDN/npm, no SRI)" — the exposure fires when this is false (a CDN script has no integrity attribute), the Magecart-style supply-chain-exposed state.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List external script tags and confirm each carries an integrity attribute.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All external scripts carry integrity='sha384-...' + crossorigin (secure / true) vs external scripts without integrity= (insecure / false)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect cross-origin script/link elements in the DevTools Elements panel for integrity + crossorigin attributes.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Elements — inspect each cross-origin <script>/<link> for integrity= and crossorigin attributes
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every external resource SRI-pinned (secure / true) vs unpinned CDN script (insecure / false)

option_description: Whether the client-side JS dependency tree is pinned via a committed lockfile (package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock) with exact resolved versions and integrity hashes.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Client-side supply-chain compromise (CDN/npm, no SRI)" — the exposure fires when this is false (unpinned/floating dependencies), allowing a compromised upstream package to be silently swapped into the build.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a committed lockfile with exact resolved versions and integrity hashes is present and is the authoritative install source.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lockfile committed with exact pinned versions + integrity hashes (secure / true) vs no lockfile / floating ranges (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN Subresource Integrity; OWASP Top 10 A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the CI build installs from the committed lockfile (e.g. npm ci / pnpm install --frozen-lockfile) rather than resolving fresh.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CI uses frozen-lockfile install (secure / true) vs unpinned resolution at build (false)

option_description: Whether automated Software Composition Analysis / dependency scanning (npm audit, Dependabot, SCA tooling) runs against the client-side dependency tree to surface known-vulnerable or malicious packages before release.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Client-side supply-chain compromise (CDN/npm, no SRI)" — the exposure fires when this is false (the dependency tree is unaudited).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run npm audit and confirm SCA gating runs in CI, reviewing all external script origins for necessity and SRI.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No high/critical advisories and every external script vetted+SRI-pinned (secure / true) vs unaudited tree / unpinned CDN scripts (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN Subresource Integrity; OWASP Top 10 A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm SCA / dependency scanning gates release on unresolved high/critical advisories in the CI pipeline.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SCA enabled and gating release (secure / true) vs no scanning (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components

option_description: Whether the CSP frame-ancestors directive is set to 'none' or 'self' — the modern primary anti-clickjacking control.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Clickjacking / UI redress" — the exposure fires when this is false (frame-ancestors absent or permissive), leaving the page embeddable in an attacker-controlled iframe.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the CSP and X-Frame-Options headers and confirm frame-ancestors is 'none' or 'self'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: frame-ancestors 'none'/'self' present (secure / true) vs absent/permissive (clickjackable / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secure Headers Project; MDN Content-Security-Policy header reference (frame-ancestors)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the CSP in DevTools for the frame-ancestors directive.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > document request > Response Headers > content-security-policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: frame-ancestors 'none' or 'self' (secure / true) vs absent or permissive (false)

option_description: Whether the X-Frame-Options response header is set to DENY or SAMEORIGIN — the legacy anti-framing fallback for older clients.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Clickjacking / UI redress" — the exposure fires when this is false (header absent); with frame-ancestors also missing, the page is framable by any origin.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the X-Frame-Options response header.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DENY or SAMEORIGIN present (secure / true) vs absent (false)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the document response headers in DevTools for X-Frame-Options.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > document request > Response Headers > x-frame-options
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DENY/SAMEORIGIN present (secure / true) vs absent (false)

option_description: Whether the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header is set to '*' (wildcard) rather than an explicit allow-listed origin. True is insecure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Overly-permissive CORS / unvalidated postMessage origin" — the exposure fires when this is true, because a wildcard ACAO lets any origin issue cross-origin reads (and exposes authenticated responses when combined with credentials).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Issue a cross-origin request and inspect the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header for a wildcard.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Explicit trusted origin only (secure / false) vs Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*' (insecure / true)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the CORS response headers of a cross-origin API call in DevTools.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > select the API request > Response Headers > access-control-allow-origin
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Explicit origin (secure / false) vs '*' (insecure / true)

option_description: Whether the server reflects an arbitrary request Origin back into Access-Control-Allow-Origin without validating it against an allow-list. True is insecure (functionally a credentialed wildcard).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Overly-permissive CORS / unvalidated postMessage origin" — the exposure fires when this is true, because a spoofed attacker Origin is echoed and granted cross-origin read access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send a request with a spoofed Origin header and confirm the server does NOT echo it into Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No reflection of evil origin (secure / false) vs Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflecting the attacker Origin (insecure / true)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Repeat the spoofed-Origin probe with several distinct fake origins to confirm none are reflected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server emits only its fixed allow-listed origin regardless of supplied Origin (secure / false) vs each fake origin echoed back (insecure / true)

option_description: Whether the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials response header is true, permitting credentialed cross-origin requests (cookies/Authorization forwarded). Only safe with an explicit validated origin allow-list.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Overly-permissive CORS / unvalidated postMessage origin" — a secondary trigger that, combined with the absence of an allow-list, exposes authenticated responses to a malicious origin.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials response header on a cross-origin request.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true only alongside a single validated origin (acceptable) vs true with wildcard/reflected origin (insecure / true firing)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the CORS response headers of a credentialed cross-origin call in DevTools.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > select the API request > Response Headers > access-control-allow-credentials
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Credentials only paired with explicit allow-listed origin (acceptable) vs credentials with permissive origin (insecure)

option_description: Whether Access-Control-Allow-Origin is emitted only after validating the request Origin against an explicit finite allow-list (with Vary: Origin). True is the secure state.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Overly-permissive CORS / unvalidated postMessage origin" — the exposure fires on its absence (is_false) when credentials are also allowed, because credentialed CORS without a strict allow-list exposes authenticated responses.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe with both a trusted and a spoofed Origin and confirm the server validates against a finite allow-list and emits Vary: Origin.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only validated allow-listed origins echoed, Vary: Origin present (secure / true) vs any origin accepted (insecure / false)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the server CORS configuration to confirm the request Origin is checked against a finite allow-list before emitting Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Finite validated allow-list in config (secure / true) vs wildcard/reflected behavior (insecure / false)

option_description: Whether every window.postMessage receiver (addEventListener('message', ...)) checks event.origin against a trusted allow-list before acting on the message.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Overly-permissive CORS / unvalidated postMessage origin" — the exposure fires on its absence (is_false), because a handler with no event.origin check lets a malicious frame/window inject or steal cross-frame data.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep client source for message listeners and postMessage senders and review their origin handling.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every message listener checks event.origin against a trusted allow-list (secure / true) vs missing origin check (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN CORS guide (postMessage origin validation note)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Code review: confirm each message-event handler validates event.origin before processing the payload.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All handlers validate event.origin (secure / true) vs an unchecked handler (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN CORS guide (postMessage origin validation note)

option_description: Whether any window.postMessage sender uses a '*' targetOrigin instead of an explicit https origin, broadcasting (potentially sensitive) messages to whatever origin occupies the target frame. True is insecure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Overly-permissive CORS / unvalidated postMessage origin" — the exposure fires when this is true, because a wildcard targetOrigin can leak the message to a hostile origin.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep client source for postMessage senders and confirm none use '*' as targetOrigin.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every postMessage pins an explicit https origin (secure / false) vs a '*' targetOrigin (insecure / true)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN CORS guide (postMessage origin validation note)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Code review: confirm no postMessage call uses '*' as targetOrigin; each pins an explicit https origin.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Explicit targetOrigin everywhere (secure / false) vs a wildcard targetOrigin (insecure / true)
how_to_obtain.source: MDN CORS guide (postMessage origin validation note)

option_description: Whether authenticated/sensitive responses (PII or token-bearing) carry Cache-Control: no-store (with max-age=0), preventing the payload from lingering in the browser disk cache, back-button history, or shared proxies.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Sensitive data cached / persisted client-side" — the exposure fires when this is false (a cacheable sensitive response), leaving PII/tokens in client/proxy caches.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request an authenticated sensitive page and read its Cache-Control header.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: cache-control: no-store (secure / true) vs public / long max-age / absent on a PII page (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secure Headers Project (Cache-Control for sensitive data)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Cache-Control response header of an authenticated/sensitive response in DevTools.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Network tab > select an authenticated response > Response Headers > cache-control
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no-store, max-age=0 (secure / true) vs cacheable (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secure Headers Project (Cache-Control for sensitive data)

option_description: Whether secret/sensitive input fields (passwords, MFA codes, account/card numbers) disable browser autofill via autocomplete=off (or autocomplete="new-password"), preventing the browser caching the secret on a shared device.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Sensitive data cached / persisted client-side" — the exposure fires when this is false, because the browser's autofill store retains the secret.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Fetch the form HTML and inspect secret fields for the autocomplete attribute.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secret fields carry autocomplete=off / autocomplete="new-password" (secure / true) vs no autocomplete attribute (insecure / false)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the rendered secret input elements in the DevTools Elements panel for autocomplete handling.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Browser DevTools > Elements — inspect password/MFA/card inputs for autocomplete=off / "new-password"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: autocomplete disabled on secret fields (secure / true) vs autofill permitted (insecure / false)

option_description: Whether the server independently re-validates all client-supplied input (types, ranges, business-rule constraints) on every state-changing/sensitive endpoint, rather than relying on client-side/UI validation.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Server relying on client-side validation / authorization" — the exposure fires when this is false, because an attacker can modify the client or call the API directly to bypass client-only validation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Replay a tampered request body via curl bypassing the UI and confirm the server rejects it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server rejects (400/422) the tampered/invalid request (secure / true) vs server accepts client-only-validated input (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS); OWASP Top 10 A03 Injection

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the endpoint handlers to confirm server-side validation exists independent of the client.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server-side validation present on every state-changing endpoint (secure / true) vs reliance on client-side validation only (insecure / false)

option_description: Whether the server enforces authentication and authorization for every sensitive action server-side, independent of the untrusted client, with no reliance on UI hiding of privileged controls.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Server relying on client-side validation / authorization" — the exposure fires when this is false, because an attacker can drive a non-browser client or replay a privileged call to reach functionality the UI merely hid.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Replay a privileged API call with a lower-privileged token, bypassing the UI, and confirm a 403.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server rejects (403/422) the over-privileged request (secure / true) vs server honors it (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS); OWASP Top 10 A01 Broken Access Control

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the authorization layer to confirm checks are centralized server-side and not dependent on UI control visibility.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Central server-side authZ on every sensitive action (secure / true) vs UI-hiding-based access control (insecure / false)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01 Broken Access Control

option_description: Whether the server honors roles, privilege flags, or authorization decisions asserted by the client (e.g. an isAdmin field in the request body, a client-supplied role header, or a client-editable JWT claim) instead of deriving them from trusted server-side state. True is insecure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Server relying on client-side validation / authorization" — the exposure fires when this is true, because the untrusted client can edit the asserted role/flag to escalate privilege.
